It stops when the negative exponentiated value of the integrated optical thickness reaches a stochastically chosen value of transmittance (i.e., when the accumulated transmittance matches $1-\zeta$) [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the description of 'Regular Tracking' found in the provided text. The text states that in regular tracking, one integrates optical thickness 'until its negative exponentiated value reaches a stochastically chosen value of transmittance.' Mathematically, the negative exponentiated value of the integrated optical thickness (tau) is exp(-tau), which is the transmittance T(t). The phrase 'reaches a stochastically chosen value' corresponds to matching this transmittance against a random threshold (often denoted as 1-zeta or similar in inverse transform sampling contexts, though the specific formula 1-zeta is more explicitly detailed in the 'Closed-form' section for homogeneous volumes, the general principle described in the claim matches the 'Regular Tracking' description in the text).
